core_philosophy.name: Calibrated Cognitive Friction
core_philosophy.definition: Designing intentional friction in autonomous defense systems to prevent automation bias and enforce Meaningful Human Control (MHC).

education.dissertation: Working memory, spatial processing, and reaction times during high-stress task interruptions

evidence: Leads organizational Human Factors strategy and design validation across core software, hardware, and AI platforms.
Authored Principles for Agentic Trust, accepted for ACM CSCW 2026 Industry Perspectives, spanning Alignment, Execution, Control, and Calibration.
Defines physical ergonomics, reach envelope modeling, anatomical safety, and mechanical fit specifications.
Defines usability criteria for system latency, auditory and visual feedback, spatial layouts, and grounds engineering targets in perceptual thresholds.
Named inventor on US Patent US-12532040-B1 for context-aware multimodal interaction architectures and received a 2023 Amazon Inventor Award.
Led a multi-year psychophysics program that replaced arbitrary engineering latency targets with human perceptual thresholds and produced $50M in operational value.
Created an objective cognitive load framework using fNIRS neuroimaging and eye-tracking.
Influenced product strategy for Echo Show and Echo Hub products serving more than 75M customers.
Performed safety-critical Human Systems Integration and validation for Lunar Gateway clinical workstations in simulated microgravity.
Applied Usability Failure Modes and Effects Analysis (uFMEA) to mitigate high-consequence use errors.
Redesigned displays and layouts using NASA-STD-3001 and MIL-STD-1472 guidance, reducing task time by 30% and eliminating critical input errors.
Ran high-fidelity simulator studies of Level 2 and Level 3 autonomous vehicle handovers using biometric, auditory, tactile, and haptic alerts, improving safety and trust ratings by 24%.
Conducted urban field studies for mobile HMI and complex spatial navigation, contributing to a 5% increase in driver retention.
